topic: Peptides your body makes: kisspeptin, the brain's puberty switch named after chocolate. KiSS-1 discovered 1996 as a metastasis-suppressor gene; named for 'suppressor sequence' with 'KI' prefix in homage to Hershey, Pennsylvania, home of the Hershey Kiss; 54-amino-acid kisspeptin-54 plus shorter kisspeptin-10, -13, -14 with the same receptor affinity (Oakley, Clifton & Steiner, Endocr Rev 2009); 2003 two groups found loss-of-function KISS1R/GPR54 mutations in families with isolated GnRH deficiency and failed puberty (de Roux et al., PNAS 2003; Seminara et al., NEJM 2003); kisspeptin neurons in the hypothalamus stimulate GnRH neurons; kisspeptin triggers GnRH-induced LH and FSH secretion (Silveira, Latronico & Seminara, Adv Exp Med Biol 2013)

Peptides Nepal

Your brain's puberty switch is named after chocolate.

Meet kisspeptin.

1996 · Hershey, USA

KISS1

Found as a gene that held back cancer spread.

Named for the town's famous Hershey's Kiss.

The peptide

Its protein is cut into kisspeptins.

The longest: 54 amino acids.

2003 · The twist

No signal, no puberty.

People with a broken kisspeptin receptor did not start puberty normally.

↓
